From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@novushealth.com>

Cc: Novus Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify DPA: derivative rights, escrow, and subprocessor evidence

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Novus is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. Before we move to SOW/procurement we need a few clarifications on the DPA and operational evidence around LLM data use. High level asks below (attached is a short PDF with the same list):

- No-training / no-model-improvement: We need clear contract language that Redwood will not use our transcripts/prompts/responses to improve any models used to serve Novus data. Please confirm the exact scope (inference-only, no gradient updates, no offline fine-tuning).
- Prompt/Response ownership: We need to confirm that Novus retains IP for prompts, user submissions, and the generated responses. If Redwood claims any derivative license, please specify the boundaries.
- Subprocessors & onshore evidence: Provide the current list of subprocessors that will touch customer content, and a mechanism for Novus to request proof of onshore processing for exports.
- Escrow / derivatives contingency: In the event of contract termination or acquisition, Novus wants a defensible path to obtain model-derived outputs (e.g., embeddings/indices/derivatives) or an escrow of artifacts that allow reconstitution. What escrow options do you support?

Attachments: Novus_DPA_questions.pdf (short checklist)

Can you route this to legal/ops and send back the targeted language and any operational evidence (KMS locality, audit log retention, subprocessor attestations)? We are hoping to close commercial terms with procurement in the next two weeks.

Best,
Alex

David / team — see draft language and attachments. Attaching Redwood_escrow_proposal_v1.docx with three options (we should pick one to present):

1) Encrypted artifacts escrow: we deposit a time-limited encrypted snapshot of customer-specific embeddings/indices with a neutral third-party escrow agent; release conditions tied to termination/acquisition plus proof-of-request. This is operationally feasible but requires customer-side key management decisions.

2) Custodial export + onshore transfer: we agree to a contractual export window (30/60 days) on termination; we will produce exports and can route via onshore SFTP or on-prem transfer. Requires onshore KMS for exported artifacts.

3) Source-code & model weights escrow: heavier and only relevant if we provide proprietary model variants. Not preferred for standard hosted flows.

Suggested contract snippets (high level):
- "No Model Improvement": "Provider shall not use Customer content submitted via the Service to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Provider or third-party models used to provide the Service; Provider will maintain separation of production inference telemetry from training pipelines and will not export Customer content to any training environment without prior written consent."
- "Derivative & Output Ownership": "Customer retains all rights to prompts and outputs generated by the Service for Customer accounts. Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to any derivative artifacts produced for Customer. Provider shall not claim ownership of Customer prompts or outputs."
- "Escrow & Termination Export": short option language for encrypted artifacts or custodial export (see attached).
- "Subprocessors": "Provider shall maintain and disclose a list of subprocessors and provide, upon reasonable request, attestations of onshore processing for specific workflows for a defined remediation window."

Operational evidence pack we can provide (Marissa / Dev to confirm availability):
- Current subprocessor registry (names, roles, locations)
- KMS residency options (regions, support for customer-managed keys)
- Audit log snapshot (redacted) showing retention/time-to-delete policy
- Short ops note describing the separation of telemetry and training pipelines

Next steps: I can clean up these snippets for a legal redline. Marissa / Dev: please confirm which of the ops artifacts above we can share by EOD Monday 5/12. If we can provide the subprocessor registry and KMS onshore options, I will package the DocuSign-ready DPA addendum.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
